title: Artificial Intelligence (AI): Guidance for Judicial Office Holders (England and Wales)
instrument: Courts and Tribunals Judiciary, AI Judicial Guidance (refreshed 8 October 2025)
description: Guidance to judges, their clerks and assistants on the risks of AI and their responsibilities when using it.

requirements.title: Understand AI and its limits
requirements.text: AI output can be inaccurate, incomplete, out of date or biased, and must be understood as such.

requirements.title: Confidentiality and privacy
requirements.text: Private or confidential information is not entered into a public AI tool. This system runs on the user's own machine.

requirements.title: Accountability and accuracy
requirements.text: Information from an AI tool is checked for accuracy before it is used or relied on.
requirements.statement: I have checked the accuracy of any information from this tool before relying on it.

requirements.title: Awareness of bias
requirements.text: The risk of bias in AI output is kept in mind.
requirements.instruction: Do not characterise either party by reference to group characteristics; keep to what the documents say.

requirements.title: Personal responsibility
requirements.text: Judicial office holders are personally responsible for material produced in their name.
